summary: HfO2 films were grown by atomic layer deposition (ALD) on platinum, iridium, and ruthenium substrates using HfCl4 and H2O as precursors in the temperature range of 200-600°C. The films exhibited a monoclinic phase, and the dielectric properties were studied, showing effective permittivity values between 11-16 and breakdown fields up to 5 MV/cm. The study focused on the growth behavior, phase composition, and electrical properties of HfO2 films on noble metal substrates.
evidence: HfO2 films were grown by atomic layer deposition from HfCl4 and H2O on atomic layer deposited 40-70 nm thick platinum, iridium, and ruthenium films in the temperature range 200-600°C. The phase formed in the 30-50 nm thick HfO2 films was monoclinic HfO2 dominating over amorphous material without noticeable contribution from metastable crystallographic polymorphs. The metal-dielectric-metal capacitor structures formed after evaporating Al gate electrodes demonstrated effective permittivity values in the range 11-16 and breakdown fields reaching 5 MV/cm.
